title: New US compute-access curbs and Nvidia's leadership turmoil spark a broad AI hardware selloff
intro: Every one of the 62 tracked names fell on Monday as Washington tightened rules on remote access to AI compute and the Treasury Secretary pressed for an outside Nvidia CEO, a day before Nvidia reports. Asia took the hardest hit, with Taiwan's index down 6% and optics, substrates, test and packaging names leading declines, while data-center REITs, utilities-linked power names and Microsoft held up best.
movers_note: Against the Nov 13 close the tracked total fell 4.51% to $26.93T (about $75B of that is TSMC's market cap restated on the source), and it is down 4.70% from the Nov 9 close a week earlier; no company rose, with Digital Realty (−0.7%), Schneider Electric (−0.8%), Constellation (−0.8%), Equinix (−1.0%) and Microsoft (−1.1%) falling least and Zhongji Innolight (−12.3%), Advantest (−11.1%), Powertech (−9.9%), Unimicron (−9.9%) and Nan Ya PCB (−9.9%) falling most.

items.headline: US issues an interim rule curbing remote access to AI compute by firms in embargoed countries
items.summary: Commerce's interim rule requires licences for AI chips and servers bound for data centers that could serve firms in embargoed countries such as China. It covers facilities above 12 million TPP (about 750 H100/H200s), gives existing operators 90 days, and rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule.

items.headline: Chip and AI stocks extend their slide as Nasdaq falls for a third session
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell 2.49%, with CNBC pointing to a report that Nvidia's board is not weighing Huang's return and Treasury Secretary Bessent's call for an Nvidia shakeup, plus the new remote-access export rule as added pressure. Micron and Intel fell more than 7% and Nvidia about 4%.

items.headline: Taiex suffers its second-largest point drop of the year as TSMC, ASE, Hon Hai and Delta slide
items.summary: Taiwan's main index fell 6.03% to 41,040.08 on worries over Nvidia's leadership, futures selling and Friday's US tech losses. TSMC lost 5.74%, ASE 8.03% and Hon Hai 9.34%, while Delta Electronics fell by the daily limit.

items.headline: Bessent urges an outside Nvidia CEO and targets suspected chip diversion through Singapore
items.summary: The Treasury Secretary called for an outside chief executive at Nvidia and said agencies backed blacklisting Singapore-based Megaspeed, suspected of routing Nvidia chips to China, adding that the decision rests with Commerce. He cited Nvidia's Singapore sales as evidence of diversion as China sales fell.

items.headline: Nvidia heads into Tuesday's results after six straight weekly declines
items.summary: Analysts expect about $109.1B in revenue and $2.47 in EPS for the quarter. The stock has erased about $1.7T over six losing weeks, and Morgan Stanley trimmed its 2027-28 data-center estimates while questions mount over neocloud financing deals.

items.headline: IMF flags more than $1 trillion of circular AI financing, mostly debt-funded
items.summary: IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said the global economy is leaning heavily on AI, with just over $1T invested in AI firms flowing back as purchase orders. UBS estimates an Nvidia financing pullback could remove $50B or more from the system.

items.headline: Taiwan approves a $9.449B Micron investment and large TSMC outbound transfers
items.summary: Approved inbound investment for January to October reached a record $20.899B, lifted by Micron's $9.449B approval for its Taiwan unit. Outbound approvals included $30B for TSMC Global and $20B for TSMC Arizona.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO this week becomes a test for the AI trade amid the chip selloff
items.summary: CNBC says traders are treating Anthropic's listing, expected to price between $70 and $78 a share, as another gauge of appetite for AI stocks after three down sessions.
